output:
I'll start by looking at the docs and package layout.

Output got truncated, so I'll read the remaining files one at a time.

I'll make the edits with a Python script.

The grep failed, so the fix script never ran and those test results are the baseline. I'll fix the script's `value` line and rerun it.

The first sed mangled the script. I'll fix the broken `X)` line.

The script ran `TEN ** last` twice on that line. I'll fix it directly.

The unit tests pass. Next I'll run `tools/check.py` and review the rules the tests don't cover.

I'll check a few of the refused records and some edge cases.

The unit tests pass, and the `convert` spot checks and the `tools/check.py` run look right. I'll write the status file.

I fixed the bugs in `/app/measure` against the docs, and all 59 unit tests now pass. `python tools/check.py` reports 0 broken records out of 171. I also spot-checked unit parsing, temperature conversion and value writing with `python -m measure convert`, and they matched the docs. `/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.

Changes, by file:
- **`table.py`:** a name that exactly matches a unit is now used as written, before any prefix split. This is why `Pa` and `ft` were being read as prefixed units.
- **`expr.py`:**
  - After a `/`, every later term in the group goes in the denominator, and a second `/` in the same group is a `ParseError`.
  - An exponent now applies to the prefix and unit together, so `km^2` is a million square metres.
  - An expression is absolute only when it is a single temperature unit with exponent 1. Inside a compound unit like `J/(g*degC)` the offset is ignored.
  - Digits are matched as ASCII only.
- **`convert.py`:** an absolute temperature converts as `(value + offset) * factor`.
- **`numbers.py`:**
  - Trailing zeros in a number written without a decimal point no longer count as significant figures.
  - Ties round to the even digit, symmetrically for negative values.
  - Rounding that carries into a new leading digit is renormalized, so 999.7 to 3 figures is `1.00e3`.
  - Digits are matched as ASCII only.
- **`records.py`:** `range` is now the largest reading minus the smallest, and precision is the fewest significant figures across all readings.
- **`report.py`:** the summary rows are sorted by dimension, then by id.

On the shipped data, `run` writes reports for the records that follow the rules and lists 13 records in `errors.json`. I checked the first 11 messages and each was a genuine rule break.

I didn't touch `/app/tests`, `/app/data` or `/app/docs`.

command_result.command: cd /app && find . -type f -not -path './.git/*' | grep -v __pycache__ | head -100 && cat docs/overview.md && wc -l measure/*.py docs/*
cd /app && cat docs/units.md docs/quantities.md docs/records.md docs/output.md docs/changelog.md; ls docs/archive tools tests data | head -50
cd /app && for f in measure/*.py; do echo "=== $f"; cat -n $f; done
cd /app && cat -n measure/dims.py | sed -n 30,60p; cat -n measure/errors.py measure/expr.py
cd /app && sed -n 40,100p docs/quantities.md; sed -n 1,25p docs/records.md; cat docs/archive/*

cd /app && sed -i 's/    value = int(digits)'"'''"'/X/' /tmp/fix.py && sed -i "s/    value = int(digits)'''/    value = int(digits) * TEN ** last'''/" /tmp/fix.py && grep -n 'int(digits)' /tmp/fix.py && python /tmp/fix.py && git status --short 2>&1 | head; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -30
cd /app && sed -n 100,125p measure/table.py; git diff --stat 2>&1 | tail -3; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | grep -E '^(FAIL|ERROR)' | head -40
cd /app && sed -i "78s/.*/    value = abs(q)''', '''    if len(digits) > sig:/" /tmp/fix.py && sed -n 76,86p /tmp/fix.py

cd /app && python - <<'EOF'
p='/tmp/fix.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("    last = e - sig + 1\nX)", "    last = e - sig + 1\n    value = int(digits) * TEN ** last''')")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
python /tmp/fix.py && python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -30
cd /app && sed -i 's/TEN \*\* last \* TEN \*\* last/TEN ** last/' measure/numbers.py && python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -30
cd /app && python tools/check.py --help 2>&1 | head; python tools/check.py 2>&1 | tail -30; cat data/units.json | head -80

cd /app && rm -rf /tmp/out && python -m measure run --out /tmp/out; echo $?; cat /tmp/out/errors.json; head -20 /tmp/out/summary.json; ls tests/fixtures; grep -n 'degC\|degF\|degR\|delta' data/units.json | head -20

cd /app && for a in '3.2 km/h' '9.81 kg*m/s^2' '0.385 J/(g*degC)' '1 cal/g*K' '1 J/kg/K' '2 m s' '5 m/(s/kg)' '1 km^2' '1 cm^3' '1 (m/s)^2' '212 degF' '100 degC' '0.25' '0.25 1' ' 5  m ' '1 1/s' '1 BTU/(lb*degF)' '1 kPa^-1' '1 m^+2' '1 kkm'; do echo "== $a"; python -m measure convert "$a" 2>&1; done; python -m measure convert '300 K' degC; python -m measure convert '5 delta_degC' delta_degF;python -m measure convert '5 K' delta_degF; python -m measure convert '100 degC' degF; python -m measure convert '5 delta_degC' degC;python -m measure convert '1 mi' km

cd /app && cat > STATUS.json <<'EOF'
{
  "status": "success",
  "summary": "Fixed the bugs in measure/ against the docs: exact-name-first unit lookup, single '/' per group with the rest in the denominator, exponent applied to prefix and unit together, absolute kind only for a lone temperature unit, (value+offset)*factor, significant-figure counting, half-even rounding with carry renormalization, range as max-min, least-precise reading for sig figs, and sorted summary. All unit tests pass and tools/check.py reports 0 broken."
}
EOF
python -c 'import json;print(json.load(open("STATUS.json"))["status"])'; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -3
